rubric.data_ink: pass - the four bars are the only data marks; the panel titles, axis labels and value labels are all that accompanies them.

findings.summary: The rendered PNG's right-hand panel title reads 'whole Newton step', but the only committed revision of this script maps the stage key whole_step to 'whole step' on line 13. The drawing script and the attached artifact therefore disagree, so the picture under review cannot be shown to be the committed script's own output: either the attachment is a stale render or the figure was drawn from a different revision of the script. The reader sees a legible title either way, so this does not hold the node, but the artifact and its script must be reconciled before the figure is treated as evidence for the landed record.

read() matches only 'STAGE_DEVICE name=<name> wall_ms=<value>' but main() calls it with name 'base' and 'head' (lines 26-27), which no stage row carries, so both dicts are empty and line 32 raises KeyError on base_values[key]. Reproduced against the cited receipts in the run directory: h200-prefix.log prints 'STAGE_DEVICE name=read|residual_and_booking|local_booking_tangent|...', never name=base or name=head, and h200-base2.log carries no STAGE_DEVICE lines at all, using 'STAGE {"median_ms": ..., "name": ...}' instead. Neither arm can be regenerated from this script, so the committed figure is not reproducible from the committed receipt path.

The collapsed arm is drawn in the feature green (#2e8b57) and the base arm in grey (#929292), but the collapsed arm is the regression: 37.86 ms against 27.83 ms on the tangent and 53.76 ms against 42.84 ms on the step. Green conventionally reads as improvement, so a reader who scans by colour rather than by the value labels can read the taller green bar as the better result in a figure whose whole point is that it got worse. A neutral or warning-toned feature colour, or grey for both arms with the change annotated, would remove the inversion.

Each panel sets its own limit from its own maximum (max(values) * 1.25), giving the left panel a range near 0-47 ms and the right near 0-67 ms. Both start at zero, which limits the damage, but equal bar heights then encode different durations across panels, so a reader comparing the panels by eye under-reads how much larger the whole step is than the tangent. One y-limit shared by both panels would make the cross-panel comparison honest.
